pageCache.pageTitle: Isbourne Valley School - Ethos, visions and values
pageCache.text:
Visions and Values
Our Vision
Isbourne Valley School is a small, friendly, caring and happy school in a beautiful rural setting. From their first day with us the children have a strong sense of belonging to our school family. Through a range of learning activities and experiences both inside and outside the classroom our children develop their confidence, self-belief and a can do attitude to all aspects of their school lives. Our aim is that all of our pupils achieve more than they ever believed possible.
Our Key Values
Friendship
Resilience
Respect
Independence
Fairness
Our Motto
Learning together inside and outside the classroom
Diary Dates
Applying for a Place

Welcome
Isbourne Valley School is a vibrant, rural primary school in the beautiful village of Didbrook in the Cotswolds.
We believe that education extends beyond the classroom and that it is important children learn both inside and outside the classroom. We have a nurturing and caring ethos which aims to develop each child as an individual. Our friendly, talented and dedicated team of teachers, support staff and governors work together to give each of our pupils the opportunity to be themselves, to thrive and to achieve.
We pride ourselves on providing wide ranging and creative learning opportunities, challenges and resources to inspire our children to acquire knowledge and skills, both academic and personal, for their futures. We believe that building children’s confidence and self-esteem will encourage their independence, motivation, self-discipline and love of learning.
Please contact us on 01242 621341 or admin@isbournevalleyschool.com to come and have a look round and see us in action.

pageCache.pageTitle: Isbourne Valley School - Wrap Around Care
pageCache.text:
Wrap Around Care
Before and after school clubs are available at Isbourne Valley School.
Before school club runs Monday to Friday from 8am. Further details are available from the school office. Spaces can be booked by emailing wraparound@isbournevalleyschool.com. The cost is £5 per session. Payment for before school club is made via Parent Pay.
After school wrap around care is provided by Atlas Camps. For details of the provision, including booking information please email info@atlascamps.co.uk or click on this link http://atlascamps.co.uk/aftercare/isbourne-valley-school/
Diary Dates
Applying for a Place

Forest School
Forest School is essentially an outdoor classroom. It is all about getting out in the woods to explore and learn. Sessions are led by a qualified Forest School Leader and provide a place for nature based learning. Each session involves specific tasks and activities through which children learn holistically and develop a range of social and personal skills that help equip them for life.
We have two Forest School areas and all of the children enjoy Forest School sessions throughout the year. During these sessions children not only use the outdoor environment to learn (whether that is in some way reinforcing something they may have been taught in another lesson or learning new concepts and skills), but are also encouraged to develop their independence, decision-making skills, teamwork and practical abilities whilst learning to care for the environment around them.
Activities can include: making dens, looking at insects, collecting sticks, tying knots, building and enjoying a campfire, whittling wood or just playing in mud!
Forest School in action

Music
We love music at Isbourne Valley School - from listening to it in all its guises to singing together, using it to support our performances, playing instruments, understanding elements of music and music making, or to enjoying workshops with musicians and professional performances. Music can change and expand our worlds; we aim to help every child find music they enjoy, be inspired, develop their listening skills and grow in confidence and resilience.

Governors
Welcome to our Governors' section. Our Governors play an important role in making sure that Isbourne Valley School provides a range of learning opportunities inside and outside the classroom to enable all children to develop their confidence and achieve more than they ever believed possible. The governing body has a wealth of experience in many areas and brings valuable skills and perspectives to the school. All of our governors are committed members of the team and are passionate about delivering the best all round education possible for every individual child.

pageCache.pageTitle: Isbourne Valley School - Meet the Governors
pageCache.text:
Meet the Governors
Mrs R Bale, Chair of Governors – Local Authority Governor
Rachel is a solicitor. She has three, now adult, children, the youngest of whom attended Isbourne Valley School. She passionately believes that all children should thrive, be supported in and celebrated for their individual personalities and strengths, enabled to enjoy learning and achieve their full potential and that school is not just about educating children in terms of subjects and curriculum, but also encouraging them to see beyond their formal education, to develop skills and to prepare for successful lives beyond school. She has been Chair of Governors since May 2016.
Safeguarding governor
Appointed by governing body
Mr J Godding - Head Teacher
Justin studied history at university in London before completing his PGCE in Nottingham. He taught history at inner city comprehensive schools in Nottingham and Derby for a number of years until he moved back to Cheltenham and changed to teaching in primary schools. He particularly enjoys maths, history and Forest School. He joined Isbourne Valley School as Headteacher in September 2016. When he is not in school he runs, cycles, swims, watches cricket and is a Leeds United supporter.
Staff Governor
Mr A Keen - Parent Governor
Alistair is a zookeeper who grew up locally. Having completed a degree in animal biology at the University of Birmingham he has worked at Birdland since 2001, becoming head keeper in 2007. Specialising in penguins, he has been fortunate enough to be involved in conservation projects both locally and internationally. He has two children, one currently in Avon class, and the other recently moved to secondary school after spending her primary years at Isbourne Valley School. Out of work he enjoys chocolate eating challenges, playing cricket, watching West Bromwich Albion, Lord of the Rings, and has an interest in dinosaurs - he loves to visit the Natural History Museum, watch documentaries and really loves Jurassic Park (the book, film and game!).
Appointed by parents
Mrs R Webber - Parent Governor
Appointed by parents
Lord Wemyss - Co-opted Governor
Appointed by governing body
Mrs P Warner - Co-opted Governor
Poppy worked at the school for 7 years, during which time she joined the governing body as the staff governor. She is currently taking some time away from her career to spend more time with her two young children. She couldn't quite cut ties with the school! Poppy has spent much of her career in primary schools and is an experienced teacher; she is passionate about all children receiving a well rounded education. She is happiest when outside, particularly with horses or anything four-legged!

Curriculum
Maths
Our aim is that all children become fluent mathematicians who have a deep and lasting understanding of both mathematical concepts and processes.
Our curriculum design teaches principles of mastery and follows a coherent and detailed sequence of essential content to support sustained progression over time.
In EYFS and KS1 we use the Glow Maths Hub Mastering Number approach which aims to develop solid number sense and to strengthen the understanding of number, and fluency, with number facts. Continuous provision activities after teaching input in EYFS provide the children with further learning opportunities. In the summer term, children prepare for moving to KS1 by starting to follow and use those lesson structures and types of questions.
In KS1 and KS2, children are taught in their own year groups so they can focus on their own specific sequence of learning. The lessons are structured to give children the opportunity to use concrete and pictorial resources to deepen their understanding, to develop their mathematical thinking and to increase their fluency. Children are encouraged to use mathematical vocabulary to explain their reasoning, to make connections between their learning and to apply their understanding to problem solving tasks.

Reading
Our aim is that all children become confident and fluent readers who see themselves as readers for both pleasure and purpose.
English, particularly reading, is at the heart of our curriculum, as it is through their use of English that our children communicate, connect and can access the wider curriculum.
Children in EYFS and KS1 have daily phonics lessons in their year groups using the English Hub's Unlocking Letters and Sounds scheme. We use the actions from Unlocking Letters and Sounds to support children’s learning until they are sufficiently confident with their phonic knowledge to stop using them. Pupils also enjoy regular guided reading sessions in small groups.
All children take home reading books matched to the phonic phase they are working on before they become ‘independent readers’ choosing books to borrow from their class libraries or our school library.
Lessons in KS2 focus on developing the fluency and expression of the children’s reading by exposing pupils to extracts of a wide variety of texts, discussing vocabulary and using a range of comprehension questions to develop skills such as retrieval, inference, summarising, prediction and explanation skills.
Children continue to take books home to enjoy, choosing from their class reading corners and the school library.
